errors.text: The proposed high-pressure hot extrusion is not the target 3D ink-extrusion route followed by hydrogen de-binding and prolonged vacuum sintering.

The thermal history is substantially incorrect: 300–500°C annealing and 1000–1200°C extrusion replace the required sequential heating, 1400°C vacuum sintering for 18 hours, and water quenching from 1500°C.
The hypothesis seeks oxygen below 100 ppm, whereas the target relies on controlled oxygen near 1.0 wt.% for interstitial strengthening while avoiding excessive alpha-HCP stabilization.
It omits the titanium-sponge oxygen getter and flowing-hydrogen de-binding environment.
Metastable beta-BCC retention is attributed to avoiding an alpha-HCP temperature window rather than to rapid quenching; slow cooling in the target produces alpha-plus-beta phases.
It does not reconstruct the sequential Ta→Nb→Hf/Ti/Zr hydride decomposition and associated in-situ alloying mechanism.
